svg.title: Tiers of Intensity Architecture
svg.desc: Architecture diagram showing matching lower-environment and production sections for the Tiers of Intensity service, including the internal Traefik load balancers used to reach the LE1 stage and Chaise production EKS pods.
svg.text: Region: us-east-1 | Deployment CD: ArgoCD | Service intent: centralized TEA Tiers of Intensity domain-score processing
Lower environments use suffixed resources; production uses the same names without environment suffixes.
SE | Shopstar | SOM publish batch events
NON PROD: AWS Account Sofa King Integrations
EKS Cluster LE1 | SNS/SQS and runtime in the Sofa King Integrations account | exact cloud identifiers omitted
SNS subscriptions deliver ProductEvents into SQS; Lambda polls queues and invokes TOI service
LE1 shared EKS platform | STAGE path shown: Lambda → internal LB → Traefik → TOI pods
See access-controlled AWS configuration for operational values
service publishes calculated results to output SNS topics
- service auth to call TOI API
EKS Cluster Chaise | Production Microservices account | exact cloud identifiers omitted
Same SNS subscription -> SQS -> Lambda -> TOI service pattern | no production suffixes
- create the same input SNS, SQS, Lambda, DLQ, and output SNS pattern
- lower environment suffixes are intentionally not used in production
- resource policies, KMS keys, retention, and redrive values still need final confirmation
Chaise EKS platform | PROD path: Lambda → internal LB → Traefik → TOI pods
See access-controlled AWS configuration for operational values
service publishes calculated results to output SNS topics
- service auth to call TOI API
Producer/consumer AWS account locations; same-account vs cross-account access; allowed principals in SNS/SQS resource policies.
Final queue retention, DLQ redrive policy, retry behavior, KMS key ownership, and whether payload classification requires stricter isolation.
Lambda trigger config TBD: batch size, reserved concurrency, timeout, service auth, and queue-depth scaling/alarms.
